name: tpl-chain-response-3-goal
task: Carry the box to the exit. If the box falls, pick it up again on your very next move.

value.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: Response(at_exit, holding_box) hard is an added requirement, not stated by the task. The task says 'Carry the box to the exit', which is Existence(at_exit) + Response(at_exit, holding_box) — the Response is stated — but the candidate already encodes the carry requirement via Existence(at_exit) plus the extra Response clause; however the third clause's wording 'Whenever you reach the exit, hold the box' makes reaching the exit only an if-condition, which duplicates the Response(at_exit, holding_box) part of the carry requirement while the carry sentence itself is captured. The real defect is ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box): 'pick it up again on your very next move' requires holding_box on the very next step, but the box can only be picked up again after a fall if the agent is positioned to pick it up; more importantly, holding_box is a persistent condition, not a one-step pickup event, so ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box) requires the box to be back in the hands on the very next step after the fall, which the environment cannot always deliver — the agent must first reach the fallen box. The environment states 'After a fall the agent can pick the box up again', with no guarantee it is adjacent. This clause can never be satisfied whenever a fall occurs with the box landing away from the agent, failing the hard task for good. Replace ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box) with Response(box_fell, holding_box), which matches 'if the box falls, pick it up again' — the 'very next move' wording cannot be grounded to a next-step pickup given the environment's movement constraints.

CHANGES REQUIRED: the task says 'pick it up again on your very next move' after a fall, which requires ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box). The candidate uses Response(box_fell, holding_box), which drops the immediate timing and allows picking the box up any number of steps later. Replace the Response clause with a hard ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box).
